basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Quod enim sequitur: Et constituam pactum illi in foedus sempiternum, et semini ejus post'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Quod enim sequitur: Et constituam pactum illi in foedus sempiternum, et semini ejus post eum, etc. Semen ejus dicit in eis qui, fidem imitando Abrahae, merentur audire a Domino: Beati qui nunc fletis, quia ridebitis (Luc. VI, 21); qualibus se jungens Apostolus ait: Nos autem secundum Isaac promissionis filii sumus (Gal. IV, 28). Specialiter autem nomen Isaac, id est risus, qui ex promissione nascitur, congruit Mediatori Dei et hominum, de cujus nativitate dixit angelus pastoribus: Nolite timere, ecce enim evangelizo vobis gaudium magnum quod erit omni populo (Luc. II, 10).
